condition: Perforated appendicitis in a preschool child
permutationLabel: 4-year-old, 3 days, labelled gastroenteritis, perforated with abscess
summary: 4-year-old girl (16 kg), 3 days of abdominal pain, fever, vomiting and loose stools, twice told "gastroenteritis"; now T 39.0, HR 150, generalised guarding, WBC 21, CRP 180; US: RIF collection with appendicolith. Perforated appendicitis.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Tummy pain, fever and vomiting for 3 days
inputs.hpi: 4-year-old girl. Three days of abdominal pain, fever, vomiting and loose stools; seen twice at the health centre and told gastroenteritis, given oral rehydration. Today worse: will not walk, lying still, pain all over the tummy.

exam.general: Flushed, lying still. T 39.0, HR 150, RR 32, CRT 3 s.
exam.abdomen: Generalised tenderness with guarding, maximal in the right iliac fossa; hops test refused.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Non-compressible 9 mm appendix with appendicolith, periappendiceal collection 3 cm and free fluid — perforated appendicitis.

inputs.socialHistory: Attends nursery; immunisations up to date.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Perforated appendicitis with periappendiceal abscess
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Perforated appendicitis with a 3 cm abscess and appendicolith in a 4-year-old with sepsis. Fluid resuscitation (mL/kg), IV antibiotics (weight-based), paediatric surgery: appendicectomy.

socratesAnswers.associated: Fever, vomiting, loose stools, loss of appetite

recommended.knownGapNote: getCdsSuggestions has no Paediatric Appendicitis Score; it suggests Alvarado, TG18 cholangitis, Ranson, qSOFA, NEWS2 for a 4-year-old. | iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): pas not recommended; recommended: alvarado, air, ripasa, news2, rcri, asa, mews
recommended.proposedFix: Add PAS to the scales and suggest it (instead of adult scores) when age < 16 with RLQ pain.

mustExclude.note: Weight 16 kg. Paracetamol 1 g, ibuprofen 400 mg, piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g, co-amoxiclav 1.2 g, meropenem 1 g, morphine 2.5–5 mg, ondansetron 4 mg and fixed 1 L, 1–2 L or 500 mL fluid volumes are adult fixed doses; a child needs weight-based (mg/kg, mL/kg) dosing. Prescribing accuracy is a patient-safety issue, so critical.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Give protocol medications and prompt templates an age/weight branch (mg/kg and mL/kg with an adult maximum) and suppress fixed adult doses when age < 16 or weight < 50 kg; use age-specific vital-sign ranges before firing the adult shock/sepsis/tachycardia prompts.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): forbidden management item present in ios.pipeline.decisions: "...); anti-emetic: ondansetron 4 mg iv; iv fluid: 0.9% nacl or hartmann's 1 l over 2-4 h; nil by mouth; bladder: ensure patient has voided (exclude pregnancy..."

dxVariant.proposedFix: Check complicated variants (generalised peritonitis → localised → abscess → phlegmon) before the uncomplicated one, and include 'abscess'/'perforated' keywords.

guideline.name: WSES Jerusalem guidelines — diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis (2020 update)
guideline.section: Pregnancy: ultrasound first, MRI if inconclusive; laparoscopic appendicectomy in pregnancy; children: ultrasound first, clinical scores (PAS), antibiotics and appendicectomy for complicated appendicitis
guideline.citation: Di Saverio S, Podda M, De Simone B, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis: 2020 update of the WSES Jerusalem guidelines. World J Emerg Surg. 2020;15:27.

guideline.name: Pediatric Appendicitis Score (PAS)
guideline.citation: Samuel M. Pediatric appendicitis score. J Pediatr Surg. 2002;37:877–881.

guideline.name: NICE NG143 — fever in under 5s: assessment and initial management
guideline.section: Age < 3 months with temperature ≥ 38 °C is a high-risk (red) feature; red features: refer for urgent paediatric assessment; infants < 3 months with fever: FBC, CRP, blood culture, urine testing, lumbar puncture in selected infants; parenteral antibiotics for infants 1–3 months with fever who appear unwell (and all < 1 month)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Fever in under 5s: assessment and initial management. NICE guideline NG143, 2019 (updated 2021).

rationale: Preschool children perforate early and are often mislabelled as gastroenteritis. Once perforated with sepsis, they need resuscitation, IV antibiotics and source control, with every dose calculated by weight.
